Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

mcqs.q: Why do some rivers form deltas and others form estuaries?
options: Deltas form on big rivers and estuaries on small ones.
Deltas form where rivers deposit sediment faster than the sea can remove it (calm seas, heavy load); estuaries form where tidal energy removes sediment (strong tides).
Because HDI is easier to calculate than GNI.
Deltas form in cold climates and estuaries in warm climates.

mcqs.q: Why is HDI a better measure of development than GNI per capita?
options: A tornado is just a small hurricane.
Because HDI is easier to calculate than GNI.
HDI combines income, life expectancy and education, capturing quality of life — GNI per capita is just average income and hides inequality and non-economic wellbeing.
Because HDI measures how happy people are.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a hurricane and a tornado?
options: Hurricanes are huge (hundreds of km) tropical ocean storms that last days; tornadoes are small (tens of metres) intense rotating columns from thunderstorms over land, lasting minutes.
A tornado is just a small hurricane.
Hurricanes and tornadoes are basically the same thing.
Deltas form in cold climates and estuaries in warm climates.
